mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a 3-month moving average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 3-month pre-trend period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) reduce consumer and business confidence, lowering expected future earnings and pushing down S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with UNRATE at the 5% significance level over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (HOUST) coinciding with strong industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust consumer and business demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next month.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% month-over-month and INDPRO exceeds 108.0
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns fail to outperform a 30-day rolling average baseline by more than 10 basis points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates weakening supply-chain activity, which raises uncertainty and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next quarter.
failure_condition: Quarterly forward returns are not statistically different from the prior quarter's average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2%, it suggests the Federal Reserve will maintain a higher policy rate for longer, which reduces equity discount rates and lowers 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during the prior 12 months with CPIAUCSL changes ≤ 2% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (PAYEMS) accompanied by rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals a softening labor market, which can erode investor optimism and drive negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by > 10% month-over-month and UNRATE increases by > 0.2% in the following month
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between PAYEMS decline and 20-day forward returns at the 10% significance level over 18 months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail activity (HOUST) without a corresponding decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests strong demand-side momentum that boosts earnings expectations and supports positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer confidence (indirect proxy via UNRATE > 5%) predicts supply-side constraints and higher uncertainty, which typically precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show a significant negative relationship with UNRATE levels above 5% (p > 0.05).
